q: The Kleene-Brouwer ordering on descriptive set theory: a tree T on ω is well-founded iff it has no infinite branches. A set A ⊆ ℕ^ℕ is Π⁰₁ (closed) in the Baire space iff:
opts: A is the set of paths through a recursive tree T
A = [T] = {paths through T} for a closed tree T (a tree closed under initial segments)
A is a finite union of closed intervals
A is the complement of an open set (in the product topology)
exp: Π⁰₁ (closed in Baire space) sets are exactly the complements of Σ⁰₁ (open) sets. In the product topology on ℕ^ℕ, open sets = unions of cylinder sets. So closed sets = complements = those that can be represented as [T] = {branches of a pruned tree T} where T is closed under initial segments.
